body.statement: For rational or algebraic primitive inputs, finite unions of closed rational intervals presenting each projected alternative coordinate, and every rational tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the handle in \(\mathrm{def{:}tolerance\mbox{-}handle}\) terminates with an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing the full-cell conditional value \(V^{\star}\), a finite outer union containing \(\mathcal{S}^{\star}\) and contained in the \(2\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set, and a finite inner union contained in the \(\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set. It asserts a unique design only when the supplied separation certificate proves uniqueness against every retained competing branch and slack-cell weight set.
body.justification: The computational statement is strong enough for design use but never asks an interval routine to decide equality of arbitrary exact real values.
body.gap: Published enrichment optimizers report numerical solutions without a theorem enclosing the full optimizer set across equality strata.
body.consumer: A protocol can archive machine-checkable value and design boxes and reserve point recommendations for explicitly separated cases.
